passage:
Friday. A visiting relative leaned down and said, "Give me a kiss!" Two-year-old Zainab hid behind her mother, Rehana, and shook her head. The relative laughed and lifted her anyway. Zainab went stiff and cried.
Saturday. When the doorbell rang, Zainab clung to Rehana's kurta.
Sunday. The relative came again. "She'll wave hello today," said Rehana calmly. Zainab waved, and the relative waved back. Zainab loosened her grip.

qa.q: What did Zainab do when the relative asked for a kiss?
qa.a: Zainab hid behind Rehana and shook her head.

qa.q: What might Zainab have felt when the relative laughed and lifted her anyway?
qa.a: She may have felt scared and upset that her no did not count, which fits her going stiff and crying.

qa.q: How did Rehana support Zainab on Sunday?
qa.a: She said Zainab would wave hello, so Zainab could greet the relative in a way she chose.

qa.q: How might the relative have seen the first meeting, and what changed on Sunday?
qa.a: The relative may have thought it was playful affection and not noticed the distress, and on Sunday a wave was accepted warmly.

grounding: Shows a toddler whose refusal is laughed at by a relative, and her mother backing her by offering a wave instead of a kiss.

passage:
At the family dinner in Vancouver, Uncle Jun scooped up Wei, two. "Give Uncle a kiss!"

Wei turned her face away and pushed. "No!"

Everyone laughed. Uncle Jun leaned closer. "Come on, one kiss!"

Wei's lip trembled.

Her mother, Fatima, stepped over and lifted her down. "She doesn't want to kiss today. Wei, do you want to wave?"

Wei waved from her mother's arms. Uncle Jun shrugged and smiled.

qa.q: What did Uncle Jun ask Wei for?
qa.a: Uncle Jun asked Wei for a kiss.

qa.q: What was Wei feeling when her lip trembled?
qa.a: Wei felt scared and upset, as if her "no" didn't count while everyone laughed.

qa.q: How did Fatima protect Wei politely?
qa.a: Fatima lifted her down, said calmly that Wei didn't want to kiss, and offered waving instead.

qa.q: How might Uncle Jun see the moment differently from Wei?
qa.a: Uncle Jun probably meant it as affection and fun, not realising Wei felt pressured and frightened.

grounding: Shows a toddler whose refusal of a relative's kiss is laughed at, and a parent who politely backs her and offers a wave instead.

passage:
Diwali. Mama picked up Rashmi, two. "Kiss your Mama!" She squirmed. He laughed. Devika said nothing, and Rashmi cried.

Next Sunday. Mama came again. "Kiss?" Rashmi hid behind Devika. This time Devika said, "She doesn't want to. Rashmi, can you say namaste?" Rashmi pressed her hands together.

Two weeks later. Mama arrived and knelt. Rashmi looked at him, smiled and said, "Namaste," on her own.

qa.q: What did Rashmi do on the second visit instead of kissing?
qa.a: Rashmi pressed her hands together for namaste.

qa.q: What was Rashmi feeling when she squirmed and cried at Diwali?
qa.a: Rashmi felt frightened and upset that her no didn't count when she was laughed at.

qa.q: What changed on the second visit, and why did it help?
qa.a: Devika backed Rashmi politely and offered namaste instead, so Rashmi learned her no mattered.

qa.q: How might Mama have seen Rashmi differently by the third visit?
qa.a: Mama seemed to learn from Devika, kneeling and letting Rashmi greet him her own way.

grounding: Shows a toddler whose refusal of a relative's kiss is laughed off, until her parent politely backs her with a namaste instead.
